paragraphs: Hilkot muqtzeh venolad beshabbat rabbim hemma, veazkir poh miqtzatam bs"d, vehu: kol keli shemmelakto lehetter, dehaynu meyuchad letashmish hammuttar beshabbat, kegon kos uqeara vekayyotze bahem, muttar letaltelo apillu shello letzorek gupo o meqomo, ella letzorek hakkeli atzmo shechoshesh alayv shello yishshaber vayganneb, umetaltelo lehatznio; abal shello letzorek kelal, asur letaltel shum keli, "p shemmelakto lehetter. udelo keharab "tosepet-shabbat" v"chesed lealpayim" dekatebu: kosot uqearot vekayyotze, muttar letaltelam apillu shello letzorek kelal, dehaiqqar lahalaka hu kisbarat haoserim, veken nireh daat mera"n za"l. velaken: adam hayyosheb al hashshulchan shealayv qearot vekosot umazleg, asur letaltel echad mikkelim ellu mikkan lekan im en lo tzorek betiltul zeh kelal, ki im raq yadayv asqaniyyot hem beeseq shello letzorek, kevan deen lo hepresh ben im qeara zo munnachat betzad zeh o betzad acher; abal im yesh lo tzorek bekak, shebbazeh yihyeh hashshulchan yapeh yoter, chashib zeh letzorek. veken adam yosheb becheder zeh, veshalach et hamsharet lehabi lo keli mecheder hashsheni, veachar kak nimlak veratza sheyyabiu lo keli acher, o kegon shettaa hashshalicha velo hebi lo oto hakkeli, veshalechu od happaam, asur letaltel keli harishon letaltelo lecheder rishon im en lo tzorek bazeh kelal mishshum shemirat hakkeli, deen lo hepresh ben im yishshaer hakkeli munnach kan hayyom, ben im yachaziruhu hayyom lecheder rishon, veken kol kayyotze bazeh.

Bammeh debarim amurim? bekelim vachapatzim, abal mine okalim umashqim vekol mine separim shemmuttar liqrot bahem, muttar letaltelam apillu shello letzorek kelal, vaapillu shello hizminam, lo bedibbur velo bemachshaba, name muttar, dela gazeru chaza"l lemigdar milleta shello yetaltelu ella raq bekelim vachapatzim, abal okalim umashqim useparim lo hayu biklal gezera zo; umikkol maqom muttar lissa hassakkin becheqo ap kesheholek lebet-hakkeneset beir sheyyesh bah erub, "p sheeno tzarik lesakkin zeh bebet-hakkeneset - epshar sheyyitztarek lah achar sheyyetze mibbet-hakkeneset, dela aseru chaza"l tiltul shello letzorek ella kesheen lo tzorek bazeh kelal kol hayyom, abal im tzarik lehishtammesh bo beshabbat, vehu noseo etzlo kede sheyyihyeh mukan umezumman lo kesheyyitztarek elayv, chashib zeh letzorek veshari. umihu, im achar sheggamar seuda shelishit veen bedato leekol od, vehu holek lebet-hakkeneset mibbeod yom kede lehitpallel arbit, asur letaltel hassakkin becheqo, deha en lo od tzorek bah beoto hayyom, shekkebar qarab haereb; veraq im noseah kede shello tignob, shari, vekannizkar leel. veayyen "machatzit-hashsheqel", siman shch, seip qatan t', yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: A utensil whose function is for a permitted purpose (intended for permitted use on the Sabbath, such as a cup or a bowl) may be handled also for the sake of the utensil itself (out of concern it might break or be stolen), but not with no need at all (mere "busy hands"). Therefore one sitting at a table with utensils should not move them around for no reason, but if there is a reason (for example, so the table looks nicer), it is permitted. Food, drink, and books permitted for reading may be handled even with no need at all, since the Sages did not impose a decree on these. It is permitted to carry a knife in one's pocket even to the synagogue (in a city with an eruv) if he might need it later that same day; but one who has already finished the third meal and has no intention of eating again, and is going to the synagogue while it is still day to pray the evening prayer, is forbidden to carry the knife in his pocket, since he has no further need of it that day; only if he carries it so that it not be stolen is this permitted.
takeaways: A utensil whose function is for a permitted purpose may be handled even just for its own preservation, but not with absolutely no need
Food, drink, and books may always be handled, even without a special need
It is permitted to carry a knife to the synagogue if it might still be needed that day, but forbidden after the third meal when there is no further need

paragraphs: Hattepillin asur letaltelam, veim rotzeh lesheb bimqoman, o kede shello yetannepu o shear bizzayon, shari letaltelam. veim yesh lo kis sheyyesh bo tzitzit vegam yesh bo kis tepillin, uba beyom-shabbat lehotzi hatztzitzit, veyetze immo gam kis hattepillin, yetaltel hattepillin al menat lesheb bimqomo veyesheb bimqomo. ubi"megillat-ester" yesh pelugta, veyesh lehorot kisbarat hammattirin.

clarification.explanation: Tefillin may not be handled on the Sabbath (they are muktzeh), except for the sake of their place (to sit there) or so that they not become dirty or disgraced. If one pouch contains both tzitzit and tefillin, and one wants to take out only the tzitzit, it is permitted to move the tefillin as well (in order to sit in their place). Regarding the Scroll of Esther, there is a dispute as to whether it is muktzeh, and the ruling should follow the lenient opinion.
takeaways: Tefillin are muktzeh, but may be handled for the sake of their place or to prevent disgrace; regarding the Scroll of Esther, the ruling should follow the lenient opinion that it may be handled

paragraphs: Keli shemmelakto leissur, rotzeh lomar shemmeyuchad limlaka haasura beshabbat, eno muttar letaltelo ella raq letzorek gupo, kegon qurenas liptzoa bo egozim veqardom lachtok bo debela, o letzorek meqomo, dehaynu shetztzarik lehishtammesh bemaqom sheoto hakkeli munnach sham, veaz muttar lo letaltelo mishsham ulehannicho bekol maqom sheyyirtzeh; abal shello letzorek gupo o meqomo, ella metaltelo mippene sheyyare pen yishshaber o yigganeb, o mechamma letzel, asur. v"p sheamarnu diltzorek meqomo metaltelo umannicho bekol maqom sheyyirtzeh, im kol zeh, im haya notelo beyad zo, asur litteno bederek hilluko beyad sheniyya, dezeh miqqere tiltul chadash, vekannizkar bapposeqim za"l.

clarification.explanation: A utensil whose function is for a forbidden purpose (intended for work forbidden on the Sabbath, such as a hammer or an axe) may be handled only for the sake of its own use (to use it itself, for example to crack nuts) or for the sake of its place (its place is needed) — but not casually out of concern for breakage or theft. Even when it is handled for the sake of its place, it should not be passed from hand to hand along the way (this would constitute new handling).
takeaways: A utensil whose function is for a forbidden purpose may be handled only for its own use or for the sake of its place, not casually

paragraphs: Qedera o shear keli shemmebashshelim bo, ap al gab delipamim notenim bah perot umishtammeshin bah shear tashmish shel hetter - la miqqere keli shemmelakto lehetter, dehaddin hu sheholekin bahem achar rob tashmishan, vekevan dezo haqqedera, rob tashmishah hu melaka haasura beshabbat, en metaltelin otah ella raq letzorek gupah o meqomah, abal im hi reqanit umittaltela mechamma letzel o kede shello tishshaber o tignob, asur; veayyen "mishbetzot-zahab", siman shch.

clarification.explanation: A cooking pot is considered "a utensil whose function is for a forbidden purpose" (even though it is sometimes used for permitted purposes too), since one follows its predominant use — therefore it may be handled only for its own use or for the sake of its place, not casually out of concern for breakage or theft.
takeaways: A pot: one follows its predominant use (cooking, forbidden), and it therefore has the law of a utensil whose function is for a forbidden purpose

paragraphs: Sakkin shel shechita o shel mila o izmel shel separim vesakkin shel soperim shemmeyuchad letiqqun haqqulmosim - kevan shemmaqpidin shello laasot bahem tashmish acher, asur letaltelam apillu letzorek gupan umeqoman, vaapillu techubim benadan im shear sakkinim, asur letaltel hannadan "p shehu basis leissur ulemotar. vehu haddin lequrenas shel besamim shemmaqpidin alayv shello yitlaklek; abal im yichadam lekol echad meellu hannizkarim meereb-shabbat limleket hetter, muttar. veken neyar chalaq, im hu chashub meod shehu meyuchad liktob bo iggerot davqa, veen mishtammeshin bo tashmish acher likrok bo ezeh dabar, dino kekelim hannizkarim veasur letaltelo.

clarification.explanation: A slaughtering knife, a circumcision knife, a bookbinder's blade, and a knife designated for sharpening quills — since one is careful not to use them for anything else, they may not be handled even for their own use or their place (even within a sheath together with other knives). The same applies to a spice hammer designated for keeping cleanliness. But if they were designated before the Sabbath for a permitted use, they are permitted.
takeaways: Designated, carefully-reserved utensils (a slaughtering or circumcision knife, a blade, a quill) may not be handled even for their own use, unless designated in advance for a permitted purpose

paragraphs: Kol maakalim sheasurim bahanaa, kegon basar bechalab vearela vekayyotze, sheeno yakol lehaakilam gam liklabim, asur letaltelam apillu letzorek gupan umeqoman. veken hu haddin beyen-nesek, apillu setam yenam sheissuro middibre soperim, dekol ellu muqtzim mechamat gupan veasur letaltelam bekol open; abal maakalim sheasurim baakila umuttarim bahanaa, kegon nebelot uterepot, o besar-op bechalab vekayyotze bazeh, kevan shehem omedim lehaakilan liklabim, muttar letaltelam kishar maakle behema. ubetza shennoleda beshabbat, veken chalab shennechelab beshabbat, uperot shennitleshu beshabbat vekayyotze bazeh, shehem omedim lemaakal adam, sheasurin laadam bo bayyom bilbad, "p sheyyakol lehaakilam liklabim o lenakerim; kevan sheen omedim lekak, ella laakilat adam achar shabbat, hare zeh asur letaltelam beshabbat apillu letzorek gupan umeqoman. veken hu haddin tebel sheasur leadam beshabbat mechamat sheeno yakol letaqqeno beshabbat, kevan shehu mukan laadam, ki tekep achar shabbat metaqqeno veokel oto, hare zeh muqtzeh mechamat gupo veasur letaltelo beshum open, v"p sheissur tiqquno beshabbat eno ella middibre soperim; umihu, dabar shennimshak issur akilato leadam gam bechol kegon hechadash, "p sheyyesh lo hetter leadam achar zeman - muttar letaltelo letzorek meqomo, o litteno libhemot o lenakerim, kevan shennimshak zeman issuro leadam zeman harbeh.

clarification.explanation: Foods forbidden even for benefit (meat cooked with milk, orlah) may not be handled at all (they are muktzeh due to their own substance), since they cannot even be fed to dogs. Wine used for idolatry, or ordinary wine of non-Jews, has the same law. Foods forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit (unslaughtered animals, torn animals, poultry cooked with milk) may be handled like any animal feed. An egg laid on the Sabbath, milk milked on the Sabbath, or fruits picked on the Sabbath may not be handled (they are only fit for human consumption after the Sabbath). Untithed produce that cannot be tithed on the Sabbath is entirely forbidden to handle. But something forbidden to a person even on weekdays (such as new grain before the omer), may be handled for the sake of its place or to give to animals or non-Jews.
takeaways: Foods entirely forbidden even for benefit (meat with milk) may not be handled; foods forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit (an unslaughtered animal) may be handled as animal feed
Something that came into being on the Sabbath (an egg, milk, a picked fruit) may not be handled all Sabbath

paragraphs: Kol dabar sheen torat keli alayv, veeno maakal adam velo maakal behema, kegon: abanim umaot veetzim veqanim veqorot veapar vechol veqemach veissa vehammet ubaale-chayyim vekayyotze bidbarim ellu; vaapillu shehu dabar sherauy lehishtammesh bo dabar hammuttar beshabbat, kegon abanim sheruyin liptzoa bahem egozim, utzerorot sheruyin lekassot bahem kelim vekayyotze bazeh, kevan sheen torat keli alehem, hare zeh muqtzeh mechamat gupo, veasur letaltelam apillu letzorek gupam umeqomam. veim yichadam letaltelam leezeh tashmish, hare zeh horid torat keli alehem, "p shehem kebedim ugedolim harbeh shetztzarik lahem asara bene-adam letaltelam.

clarification.explanation: Something that has no "status of a utensil" and is not food (stones, coins, wood, dirt, a corpse, live animals) is muktzeh due to its own substance and may not be handled even for its own use or its place, even if it is fit for a permitted use (like a stone for cracking nuts). But if it was designated in advance for some use, it acquires "the status of a utensil" and is permitted, even if very heavy and large.
takeaways: "Raw" objects (a stone, wood, dirt) are muktzeh even if useful, unless designated in advance for a use

paragraphs: Kelim haomedim lischora, "p sheen regilin lehishtammesh bahem shum tashmish, mikkol maqom, im eno maqpid alehem millehishtammesh bahem, en lahem din muqtzeh leaseran betiltul, yaan kevan deeno maqpid millehishtammesh bahem, hare zeh lo hissicha dato mehem legamre millehishtammesh bahem, abal im maqpid alehem millehishtammesh bahem tashmish acher kede shello yipchatu demehem unetanam leotzar, hare ellu muqtzin vaasurin betiltul apillu letzorek gupan umeqoman, vekol shekken letzorek atzman mechamma letzel, kevan demaqpid alehem vegam netanam leotzar; mihu, kelim haomedim lischora udemehem yeqarim - "p shello netanam leotzar, asur letaltelam, ella im ken yichadam mibbeod yom letashmish. vekitbe haqqodesh veakkilyan umashqin, "p shemmeyuchadim lischora velo hizminam mibbeod yom, lo bemachshaba velo bedibbur, muttar letaltelam.

clarification.explanation: Utensils intended for sale — if one is not careful about them being used normally, they may be handled (his attention has not been entirely diverted from them). If one is careful not to use them (so as not to harm their price) and put them into storage, they are muktzeh and forbidden even for their own use or place. Expensive merchandise utensils are forbidden even without being put into storage, unless designated in advance for permitted use. Sacred books, foods, and beverages may be handled even if intended for sale.
takeaways: Merchandise utensils may be handled if one is not careful about their normal use; if careful and stored away, they are forbidden

paragraphs: Dabar sheeno keli, ella sheyyesh alayv torat keli mechamat sherauy lehishtammesh bo ezeh tashmish beshabbat, kegon gizzin shel tzemer sheruyin lehissamek uleshabbat alehem vekayyotze bazeh - im hiknisam leotzar lischora, bittel torat keli mealehem veasur letaltelam "p sheeno maqpid alehem millehishtammesh bahem, ella im ken chazar veyichadam letashmish leolam.

clarification.explanation: An object that is not a utensil but has "the status of a utensil" because it is fit for use (such as wool fleece to sit on for the Sabbath) — if it was put into storage for sale, the status of a utensil is nullified from it and it may not be handled, unless it is designated anew for permanent use.
takeaways: An object that acquired "the status of a utensil" through use, and was then returned to merchandise, loses its status and is forbidden until designated anew

paragraphs: Kol hakkelim shennishberu apillu shennishberu beshabbat, muttar letaltel shibrehem im reuyim leshum melaka, kegon lekassot bahem hechabit o pi hapak vekayyotze, abal im en reuyim leshum melaka, asur letaltelam. veim nishberu bemaqom sheyyekolin lehazziq, kegon shehem kele zekukit, muttar lepannot hashshebarim kede shello yizzoqu bahem, ak shibre keli cheres sheen mazziqin lehaddores alehem, asur lepannotam; v"p shebbene-adam doresim alehem veal yede kak mishtabberim yoter "y derisa - en bekak kelum, ki hu dabar sheeno mitkavven. veha deamerinan demuttar letaltel hashshebarim im reuyim leshum melaka, haynu davqa keli shennishbar kullo, abal im lo nishbar kullo ella raq chatika mimmennu, vaadayin hakkeli meshammesh tashmisho harishon, en chatika zo shel hashsheber mutteret betiltul ella im ken hi atzmah adayin reuya qetzat letashmishah harishon, abal im enah reuya letashmishah harishon, "p sheruya letashmish acher, kegon lekassot bah keli vekayyotze, hare zeh asur letaltelah demiqqere "nolad", kevan denishbera min hakkeli beshabbat atzmo; velaken im nishbera bechol, az muttar letaltelah beshabbat im reuya leshum tashmish, "p sheenah reuya letashmishah harishon, v"p sheatta beshabbat en lo tzorek lehishtammesh bah, im kol zeh, kevan dehi reuya leezeh tashmish, muttar letaltelah; veraq im zeraqah laashpa mibbeod yom, asur letaltelah beshabbat "p sheruya leshum tashmish, dekevan dizraqah laashpa, bittelah mittorat keli veneesra betiltul lekol adam apillu laaniyyim, deazelinan bazeh batar habbealim; mihu, zeh davqa im zeraqah laashpa mibbeod yom, abal im zeraqah laashpa beshabbat, muttar letaltelah, hoil vehaya aleha torat keli beben-hashshemashot shehu techillat kenisat hashshabbat.

clarification.explanation: Broken utensils (even broken on the Sabbath itself) — their fragments may be handled if they are fit for some task (such as covering a barrel); if the fragments are fit for nothing, they may not be handled. Glass fragments that might cause injury may be cleared away; harmless pottery fragments may not. A broken piece no longer fit for its original use, but only for another use, that broke on the Sabbath itself, is forbidden (it is considered "newly created"); but if it broke during the week, it is permitted (it already had the status of a utensil from before the Sabbath), unless it was thrown into the trash before the Sabbath (thereby nullifying its status). If it was thrown into the trash on the Sabbath itself, it may be handled, since it had the status of a utensil at twilight.
takeaways: Fragments of utensils fit for use may be handled; fragments that broke on the Sabbath itself into a wholly new use are forbidden ("newly created"), unless they broke during the week

paragraphs: Lo ameru "kol sherauy lekassot bo keli, yesh torat keli alayv" ella raq beshibre kelim, hoil vehaya alehem kebar torat keli keshehayu shelemim, ulekak gam achar nishberu lo paqa mehem torat keli im hem reuyim letashmish shel kissuy vekayyotze, abal tzerorot o abanim vachatikat etz vekayyotze, asher meiqqaran lo haya alehem torat keli gamur, "p sheruyim letashmish lekassot bahem kelim, lo yihyeh alehem bishbil zeh torat keli; velaken, kol shello yichadam mibbeod yom letashmish zeh, asur letaltelam apillu letzorek gupam umeqomam vekaasher katabnu leel.

clarification.explanation: The rule "anything fit for covering has the status of a utensil" applies only to fragments of utensils (which already had the status of a utensil when whole), but not to objects that were never a complete utensil at all (stones, plain wood) — these remain muktzeh unless designated in advance for use. Anything not designated before the Sabbath for such use may not be handled even for its own use and place.
takeaways: Raw objects (never a utensil) fit for covering do not automatically acquire "the status of a utensil" — only fragments of former utensils do

paragraphs: Machat shelema sheqqorin bearbe "ibre" (machat tepirat yad) shemmelaaktah leissur, litpor bah, muttar letaltelah beshabbat kede lachtzotz bah shinnayv o littol bah haqqotz kedin keli shemmelakto leissur demuttar letaltelo letzorek gupo kemo shekkatabti leel; ubilbad sheyyizzaher sheyyittol haqqotz benachat shello yotzi dam, deyesh bazeh issur chobel. veim i epshar lehotzi haqqotz bilti hotzaat dam, asur, "p sheeno mitkavven - mishshum pesiq resheh velo yamut. bema debarim amurim? bemachat shelema sheyyesh torat keli aleha, abal im nittal chuddah o nipgam chor shellah sheenah reuya limlaka, hare batel torat keli mealeha veomedet lizriqa, veasur letaltelah kede littol qotz o lachtzotz shinnayv; veraq im yichadah mibbeod yom letashmish zeh, naaseh aliyya torat keli umuttar letaltelah.

clarification.explanation: A whole sewing needle (a utensil whose function is for a forbidden purpose) may be handled for its own use (to pick between teeth or remove a splinter), provided the splinter is removed gently without drawing blood (the prohibition of wounding); if it cannot be done without blood, it is forbidden. A damaged needle no longer fit for sewing loses the status of a utensil and may not be handled, unless designated in advance for another use.
takeaways: A whole needle may be handled for its own use (removing a splinter, without blood); a damaged needle is muktzeh unless designated in advance

paragraphs: Shiyyure machtzelaot shebbalu, "p sheen reuyim lesheb alehem, muttar letaltelam, dela nipqa shem keli shehaya alehem techilla, hoil degam atta reuyim lekassot bahem tinnup. veim zarqam laashpa mibbeod yom asur letaltelam. umatlaniyyot shehem shiyyure begadim shebbalu: im en bekol achat mehen shelosh etzbaot al shelosh etzbaot, asur letaltelan, mippene sheen reuyim lo laaniyyim velo laashirim, veim yesh bahem shelosh etzbaot al shelosh etzbaot vehem shel ani - im lo zarqam laashpa, muttarim kol haaniyyim shebbaolam letaltelam, diruyot lahem laasot telay bebigdehem, abal haashirim, asur letaltelam, ella im ken hi shelsha tepachim al shelsha tepachim, deaz hi reuya gam laashirim; mihu, im heashir yosheb bebeto shel oto ani baal hammatlit, az apillu im hi raq shelosh etzbaot al shelosh etzbaot deenah reuya laashirim, muttar oto ashir letaltelah, yaan dehu nigrar achar baal habbayit shehu ani sheruya lo, denimtza reuya zo beoto habbayit; veim hammatlit hi pachot mishshelosha tepachim al shelosha tepachim, vehi shel heashir deenah reuya lo, az hi muqtzet gam laaniyyim, deazelinan batar habbealim vechashebinan lah keillu nizreqa laashpa. vachatikat tallit shel metzuvveh, "p shehi gedola, asur letaltelah, mippene sheen mishtammeshim bah tashmish shel chol.

clarification.explanation: Remnants of a worn-out mat may be handled (still fit for covering filth), unless thrown into the trash beforehand. A rag (a remnant of clothing): if smaller than three by three fingerbreadths, it is forbidden to everyone. Three fingerbreadths or larger, belonging to a poor person, is permitted to all poor people (fit for a patch); for wealthy people it is forbidden, unless it is three by three handbreadths. A wealthy person sitting in a poor person's house who owns the rag may handle it (following the host). A wealthy person's rag smaller than the measure is muktzeh even for poor people (one follows the owner). A piece of a tallit used for a commandment is forbidden to handle, since it serves no weekday use.
takeaways: The measures for rags depend on their size and the identity of the owner (poor/wealthy) — what matters is whether they are actually fit for use by that owner

paragraphs: Muttar lehaabir meal hashshulchan perurin sheen reuyin ella libhema uleop, veken muttar lehaabir atzamot uqelippin hareuyim libhema, abal qelippe egozin usheqedim vekayyotze, sheen reuyim libhema, asur lehaabiram uletaltelam beyadayv o "y keli, vegam asur letaltel hashshulchan beodam alayv kede lenaaro bachutz. ketzad yaaseh? yetaltel hashshulchan kesheyyesh alayv chatikat pat vinaaru bachutz, lepi sheqqelippin ellu betelim legabbe happat, vekevan shehappat odennu al hashshulchan, yukal letaltel hashshulchan. veim hu tzarik limqom hashshulchan, hare zeh metaltelo umenaaro bachutz "p sheen alayv pat ella qelippin ellu lebaddam. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" heeleti bs"d, dedavqa legabbe pat betelin qelippin ellu, abal legabbe qelippin vaatzamot sheruyim lemaakal behema davqa, la bateli.

clarification.explanation: It is permitted to clear from the table crumbs, bones, and peels fit for animal or poultry feed. Nut and almond shells (not fit for animals) may not be handled directly, but the entire table (with these shells on it) may be handled when bread is also on it (the shells are nullified in relation to the bread — and specifically bread nullifies them, not bones or peels fit for animal feed), and shaken out outside. If the place of the table is needed, it is permitted to handle it and shake it out even without bread on it.
takeaways: Peels not fit for animals are handled indirectly — via bread on the table (specifically bread, not bones or peels fit for animal feed), or because the table's place is needed — never directly

paragraphs: Haatzamot, "p shemmuttar letaltelam mishshum dachazu liklabim, haynu davqa bemaqom dishkichi kelabim, abal bemaqom dela shekichi kelabim kegon sheholek bispina o beshayyara bammidbar, asur letaltelam. vegarine temarim, beirenu maakilim otam libhemot, deokelim otam haizzim, lekak muttar tiltelam. uqelippe betzim asurim betiltul, "p deomerim deokelim otam hattarnegolim, la mehanne zeh; chada, deyesh omerim sheen okelim ella qelippe betzim sheenam mebushshalim velo hambushshalim; veod, "p sheokelim otam, mazziqe lehu, ubaal habbayit qepid veeno rotzeh sheyyoklu otam, velaken asurim betiltul; vedame zeh ledin besar dag sheeno malucha, deasur letaltelo ap al gab dachaze lachayya ubehema, mippene dehaadam qepid shello yaakil dabar harauy laadam - libhema vechayya, vehu haddin haka; kak heeleti bsh"q "mqbtzl", bs"d.

clarification.explanation: Bones are permitted to be handled (fit for dogs) only in a place where dogs are actually present (not on a boat or a caravan in the desert). Date pits (which goats eat in the area) are permitted. Eggshells are forbidden to handle, since they are not eaten even when cooked, and the homeowner does not want human food fed to animals (like unsalted fish meat).
takeaways: The permission to handle "animal feed" depends on animals or dogs actually being available in the place, and on the owner not minding feeding human food to animals

paragraphs: Kol dabar sheasur letaltelo, asur litteno betok keli, mishshum dehave mebattel keli mehekano; velaken asur lehannicha keli al hashshulchan kede lehannicha bo qelippe betzim o qelippe egozim vekayyotze, sheen reuyim lemaakal adam; vedavqa im keli zeh hu reqan sheen bo dabar harauy lemaakal adam.

clarification.explanation: Something forbidden to handle is also forbidden to place inside a utensil (since this "disqualifies the utensil from its use"); therefore it is forbidden to place an empty vessel on the table in order to put eggshells or nutshells into it (which are not fit for human food).
takeaways: One should not place a muktzeh item inside an empty vessel — this "disqualifies the vessel" from its purpose
